# Peer review — x-ai/grok-4.7, persona: grinchy

Verdict: major revision. Not ready to be the contract for a citable release. The documentary spine is sound enough to keep building a cut-down M2 against, but several rules contradict each other, several cannot be stored or tested, and the trust model does not support the users named in Requirements §1 and §3.1.

I am treating truncated second columns in the extracted tables (requirements map, check-outcome columns) as extraction loss, not as missing spec text, unless the prose itself never states the rule.

## 1. Internal coherence

1. The human-review rule is self-contradictory. C1 and Q5 forbid routing any class of items to the author and say no person reviews high-impact items; the only human check is held-out reference answers. Q17, Fusion §3 and Storage §4 then require lines read by hand, match judgements decided by hand, and tier-2 candidates “reviewed by hand”, and name the author as the only person (C1). Fusion §3 also “raises a chain of three as a conflict for review” and never says who reviews it once the author is forbidden to take a queue. Fix: one decision table with a closed mandatory-human set, and delete “reviewed by hand” everywhere else.

2. Requirements §2.4 says a disagreement is never left standing. It is. Language retires “source”; Ontology §2 keeps `secondary_source` and calls the rename a proposed schema change. Ontology §2 retrieval statuses include `not_published` and `not_applicable`, then says those are not fetch outcomes and that the join to Collection §3 verdicts is a proposed schema change. F8’s test cannot be run until that join exists. Fix: one status list, one column, ticket 1702 closed in the spec before it is “reviewed”.

3. The normative in-force rule and the enforced rule differ. Storage §1 states the new supersession rule, then admits the DDL still implements the old one. A validator that does not implement the rule does not test it. Fix: the DDL change is part of the rule, not a footnote; until it lands, Q2/Q7/F10 are unmet by the spec’s own milestone rule (Requirements §2.2).

4. Restatements have no home. Extraction §8 and F4 require a restatement linked to its origin, counted apart from corroboration. Storage §1’s tables and target-schema list contain no restatement relation. `same_as` is the wrong relation. The F4 test is therefore not implementable. Fix: a `restates` row with origin line id, retrieval id and adapter version, or drop the claim.

5. Multi-heading notes are specified and then deferred. Extraction §3–§4 allow several governing headings; Storage §1 stores one `groups` value until a target table exists, and says a line then sees only the nearest heading. Method notes that condition money (pro-rating, FX) can be dropped on the way into M2. Fix: `line-groups` is M2 DDL, not a target.

6. IPCC bins are not a measurement scale, so Q5’s calibration test is undefined. Fusion §1 copies Mastrandrea et al. 2010, whose likelihood ranges overlap (`likely` 66–100 and `very likely` 90–100; `unlikely` and `very unlikely` likewise). “Observed precision of each term” cannot be computed on overlapping bins. A conjunction of an overlapping probability word and an ordinal confidence grade (Fusion §3, Results §3) is not a false-positive rate. Fix: disjoint numeric bins, or a single probability with a published reliability diagram; stop calling overlapping IPCC words a calibrated scale.

7. “Statement” still means two steps. Language, Extraction and Fusion use it for D2; Presentation’s Statements page is D3. F1 nails it to the line, but agents under Q18 will implement the wrong step. Fix: the word “statement” is banned in normative sentences; say line or observation.

8. DA1 cannot represent a joint document. One country column, plus `GLB` for method sources, forces a two-country IPG text into one country or into “no recipient”. Fix: country membership as rows, not a single required column.

9. Comparator lines sit in `lines` with no validator exclusion. DA2 says 10,452 of 13,092 lines are CRS/IATI/World Bank. DA10 and F13 say they never enter a strict figure. That constraint is prose, not a Storage §1 check. Fix: a check that fails a strict-scope export containing a comparator document type or a non-strict scope.

10. Principles overclaim relative to the requirements that correct them. Requirements §4 says every released result is reproducible from the frozen release and the recorded methods. Q4 and Q8 correctly say an LLM reading is not reproducible, only its stored output, and a third party can inspect only where a public copy exists. Fix: rewrite the principles paragraph to the Q8 standard so a data paper cannot cite the stronger sentence.

11. N4 and Fusion §1 (“no rule selects or merges on its own”) are already qualified in Fusion §3 by adopted-rule programs. Leave the qualification in §1, or the two sections will be implemented as different systems.

12. F26 is M4 while the citation-critical dates are M3b. Results §4 publishes five dates (knowledge cutoff, world time, discovery cutoff, newest document date, publication date). Readers get them before plain-language definitions exist. Fix: move the five date glosses to M3b; keep the rest of F26 at M4.

## 2. Fitness for purpose

The stated product is a record negotiators can use because neither side wrote it (Requirements §1). One researcher, LLM judgements he configured, and his own book on the “USD 300 billion promise” falsify that sentence. The design rule in §1 is narrower and defensible; the outcomes bullet is not. Q16’s test is a banned-word search, which does not detect selection bias, threshold shopping, or a tally page that buries the agree-but-wrong rate.

OBS-1 asks what was pledged, signed and disbursed. Fusion §7 then makes an exact account fail closed unless coverage is judged complete, currencies match, and no interval straddles a boundary. That is the right scientific behaviour and the wrong unspoken product. There is no acceptance criterion for how many headline questions may remain blocked. A release can pass every stated check and not answer the question the Observatory exists to serve. Fix: pre-register that the headline number is the publisher’s dated figure or the cautious-threshold sum, never an inclusive sum; reconstruction residuals are a separate table; a release note states the share of agreements with no exact closing.

Results §3’s inclusive default counts matches that are “about as likely as not”. The range is honestly not a confidence interval, but nothing forces the cautious figure to be the one in the first column. Journalists will quote the larger number. Fix: cautious is the served figure; inclusive is a sensitivity annex.

Known-item recovery (Collection §5–§6) is carefully named and its upward bias is stated. The gate then ignores both the bias and the Wilson lower bound: 36/40 is “90%” with an interval that can sit near 77%, and the list may already be mostly round-zero holdings. Nothing requires a minimum of not-yet-held items. A campaign can be declared successful while mostly rediscovering the 392 documents already in hand. Fix: freeze the list with a pre-registered minimum of items absent from round zero; gate on the lower bound, or drop the 90% gate and publish the estimate only.

There is no numeric quality bar that blocks a release. Q5 requires calibration to be published, including an agree-but-wrong rate, and then allows the release anyway. For these users, a citable total with a published 30% agree-but-wrong rate is not a success. Fix: pre-register release-blocking floors (cautious-threshold precision, blocking recall, agree-but-wrong upper bound) on a gold set large enough to estimate them.

F21 excerpts and codebook work sit outside the ledger, which is right, but the ledger never records which excerpt set a paper used except via the product’s quotation list (Results §8). That list is M3b and “not served”. Researchers reproducing a coding (DP-4, LP-1) need it in the deposit. Fix: the quotation list is a release file.

Coverage of neighbours (Requirements §1) is too thin for a dataset that claims to differ by unit of record. Climate Funds Update, ODI, SEI Aid Atlas, IISD/E3G JETP tracking, and the OECD provided-and-mobilised accounting rules are the actual comparators users will set this against. Fix: a one-page “what we will not reconcile to” in the M3a report, naming those series and the rule that forbids silent alignment.

The spec is over-built against its own §2.3. ODEM branding, a PROV mapping with no engine (Ontology §0, export at M4), SKOS mapping strength on every crosswalk, depth-one equality as a theorem about non-composing likelihoods, display-occurrence records that are never served, and a readings journal of full raw responses are defensible later. They are not needed to extract the 115 pending snapshots correctly. Requirements §2.4’s “specification complete before extraction code” fights the stated “works first” constraint: Storage §1’s target list is long enough that M2 requirements are unmet by the milestone rule itself. Fix: an M2 in-force schema, and a rule that a section tagged M2 which depends on a target column is not a rule yet.

## 3. State of the art

What is aligned and should not be rewritten into RDF: append-only snapshots addressed by hash; transaction time (`recorded_at`) separated from valid time (timings); correction as a new citable object; DataCite via Zenodo; Frictionless as the descriptor; IATI transaction types, OECD DAC purpose codes, ISO country codes, OC4IDS and GEM as external lists; ROR/LEI/Wikidata as 1:1 party keys when the scheme is declared 1:1; B-cubed named as the cluster metric; FAIR applied to the release and explicitly not to the working ledger. Rejecting LinkML/OWL/SHACL until a consumer exists (Ontology §5) is the correct call.

Where it contradicts or ignores practice:

Entity resolution. Fusion §3 reinvented a pairwise LLM matcher and cited none of Fellegi–Sunter, active learning, or the usual failure modes (blocking as the recall ceiling, transitive closure creating false merges, cluster metrics that look fine while money merges are wrong). Depth-one `same_as` avoids a real bug, transitive closure of uncertain links, and substitutes an unspecified conflict queue. On the CIPP example already in Storage §4 (437 lines against 1,142, literal name intersection 3), that queue is the product. Fix: blocking recall is a release gate; conflicts are either human-closed or excluded from every sum; asset matching tries GEM and utility identifiers before any LLM proposer.

Uncertainty. NUSAP-as-prose (Fusion §1) is better than a fake pedigree score. What is missing is propagation. A computed sum can look exact while extraction error, unmatched occurrence, and FX refusal are only adjacent notes. The matching range is correctly labelled non-probabilistic (Results §3, Presentation). It does not carry the calibration error onto the total. Fix: every Observer-calculated money figure carries n, the method version, and the held-out error rate of that method, with the interval.

LLM-as-judge. Independent families, frozen prompts, held-out gold, locator checks, and a planted injection (Extraction §6.3, §12) match the better end of current practice. The spec ignores position and self-preference when the arbiter is shown both answers, treats “different family” as independence while noting shared training data only as a caveat, and maps raw self-scores onto verbal probabilities, which is not calibration. Calibration is the held-out contingency table; self-scores are a feature, not a probability. The stratum rule makes this fatal: fewer than 30 items is uninformative, strata are country × language × classification (Extraction §6.3). Four countries, four languages and thirteen classifications cannot be filled from roughly 2,640 non-comparator lines, most of them not hand-labelled. The published calibration will be a table of “uninformative”. Fix: coarsen to language × method × measure-vs-not, publish Wilson intervals on the agree-but-wrong rate, and do not print a likelihood word the gold set cannot support.

Provenance and bibliographic models. The PROV table (Ontology §0) has no `wasInvalidatedBy`, no role on derivation, and is unchecked until an M4 RO-Crate option. That is a sketch, not a mapping. Documents are not described in any bibliographic model: FRBR/LRM would have separated work, expression (translation, revision) and manifestation (re-export, mirror). Fusion §3’s content check is a reasonable substitute, but `edition_of` is doing duty for both a new expression and a new issue of a series. A citation to a line has no CSL/BibTeX object, so papers will invent citations. Fix: a release-level CSL-JSON record per principal document; leave PROV until a consumer exists, and delete the claim that the chain “maps onto” PROV.

Bitemporal design is ahead of most tracker projects, then left half-implemented. Line-referent and relation `recorded_at` are targets, and F10 depends on them. CSV-in-git is justified as review-by-diff (Storage §3) while Q5 and Operation §4 say nobody reviews rows and an LLM samples chains. Those cannot both be the reason for the storage engine. Fix: say plainly that git is the audit log, not the review surface; row review is the readings protocol plus the gold set.

FAIR. F28–F32 are the right subset. Interoperability stops at “codes follow external standards”. There is no machine mapping from local line classifications to an external concept scheme that a harvester can use, and SKOS export is M4 and values-only. Acceptable if F31 is narrowed to identifier standards. Do not claim full FAIR interoperability in the data paper.

## 4. Implementation realism

The budget model contradicts the protocol. Operation §7.1 prices an M2 pass at USD 15–30 from a prototype at USD 0.03–0.08 per document. That prototype is not two local readers plus a hosted arbiter on every disagreement, on parts, with repair calls. The runbook still serves one Qwen3.8-27B on both GPUs. The 12 GB card can host only a much smaller second “family”. Asymmetric readers on Vietnamese and Indonesian legal text will disagree often; Extraction §6.3 then sends every disagreement to OpenRouter. The 950,000-character PDF is already beyond the local context and must be parted. USD 3 per document and USD 20 per run will not survive that. USD 150 per month (Operation §7.2) against DA11’s tenfold growth plus weekly living-document snapshots is a stop, not a budget. Fix: measure arbiter rate and tokens on ten hard documents (one scan, one Vietnamese plan, one living HTML shell, one register, one French legal text) before any more protocol text; set the cap from that measurement; if the cap cannot cover the protocol, the protocol is illegal under C4.

Discovery is confounded by the same cap. Collection §5 pre-registers a stopping rule. Nothing says a monthly LLM ceiling that aborts triage is “stopped by cap” rather than protocol completion, or that recall is then void. Fix: money stop before frame coverage invalidates the campaign; it is not a quiet tail.

M3b is not a slice. Results §13 binds observations, two-threshold matching, accounts, CRS/IATI gaps, excerpts, a full deposit, redistribution review and an Observatory to one milestone. One person will not finish it as specified, and C8 will be used to drag all of it forward. Fix: split into extract-and-cite lines, then match, then accounts. Accounts that cannot close are not a reason to block a citable line release.

Human load does not disappear under C1; it concentrates on gold data the design cannot produce. Hand-labelling enough items for even a coarsened calibration, plus principal-reference checks, is the real M2 critical path. Pretending it is zero makes the schedule a fiction. A feasible load is small: the four principal references (F24), Decision 458 (Extraction §6.4), every conflict chain that would move a cautious total, and a seeded audit sample. That is days, not “review every row”. The spec forbids exactly that set.

Sharding, tmux, uv PATH, and a 512 KB hook (Storage §1, Operation §15) are workable on padme and are also a tax. The readings journal plus per-document field files will hit the hook immediately. Dolt-at-M4 should be pulled forward if the first assisted run cannot open a reviewable PR. Do not add another ontology table before that run exists.

## 5. Dead angles

Legal sequencing is behind the build. The legal note is right that acquiring, mining, retaining, sending abroad, republishing and licensing are different acts, and that it is not advice. Operation then uploads snapshot bytes to Zotero at M2 (third-party retention; R122-24 / R122-23 II) and sends text to OpenRouter at M2, while the agreements are an M3b go-live item (Legal note §1, §4; Operation §5). Zenodo deposit of verbatim labels and plan tables is publication even if the website is dark. The note’s own high branch is unlicensed re-serving of a substantial part of a protected database (Legal note §2); the document-rows view is that extraction. GitHub visibility of `data/jetp/` is unspecified. If `main` is public, the redistribution gate in Results §7 is already bypassed. Fix: private repo until the per-table assessment; no Zotero byte upload and no hosted call until the CNRS agreement exists; local-only arbiter until then, or no arbiter; Zenodo gets hashes and Observer-written tables first, verbatim columns only after the assessment. Dedicated public-registration accounts, not an institutional session that may see more than the public (F27, Legal note §1).

The non-blocking personal-data screen (Results §5) can ship signatory names and, in prose fields, people who are not signatories. Controller is unidentified (Legal note §3). That is acceptable only while the ledger is private. It is not acceptable on gh-pages.

Single points of failure: one person, one workstation, one NVMe (mitigated by restic and Zotero, the latter legally blocked), one shared `llama-server` that runs must not reconfigure (Operation §2), GitHub as the only control plane, and LLM review of LLM output as the data gate (Operation §4). The handover note (Operation §9) is necessary and late if it waits for the first DOI: write it before the first hosted call. A cross-family PR reviewer who is the same maker as the arbiter is not the check Q19 thinks it is. Fix: the data-PR reviewer is a different maker from every model that wrote the rows.

Drift to 2030. Model death is handled (Extraction §6.3). Layout drift fails closed, which is right, and will stall series. Link-rot checks are M4 (Operation §11) while papers will cite M3b. Bytes held only on padme, with redistribution forbidden, become unverifiable the day the publisher deletes the page. Fix: Internet Archive capture of every admitted URL at fetch time, M3a, not M4.

Horizon versus the question. C10 ends by default in 2030; Senegal’s period runs to 2028; CRS/IATI lag is one to three years (Requirements §1, Collection §1). F19’s announced-versus-reported gap for the end of the partnerships, especially Senegal, falls after the archive date. Stopping is honest only if F19 is scoped to flows whose reporting year is inside the horizon. Otherwise the final release will be read as a disbursement verdict the comparators cannot yet support.

A partner can poison the record. Readers are untrusted-input aware (Extraction §6.3), which is good, and white-on-white text is deferred to M4 (Extraction §5). Hidden text in a plan PDF is in scope now. The planted-instruction fixture is one document, not a rate. Fix: the M4 hidden-text fixtures move to M2 for PDF text-layer versus rendered-page disagreement on principal references; do not claim the injection test generalises.

Neutrality will rot without an external reader. No editorial board, no second institution, no obligation to publish a refused correction in a way a publisher can cite. F25’s ticket trail is good. Add a served corrections table at M3b, not M4, or the “publishers can correct” outcome is invisible for the first year of citation.

## Five changes, in order

1. Rewrite the trust model. Mandatory human verification of a closed set (principal references, the held scan, conflict chains that move a cautious total, a seeded audit). Disjoint probability bins. Coarsened strata the gold set can fill. Release-blocking numeric floors. Delete C1’s claim that no class is reviewed.
2. Make the M2 schema able to store the M2 rules: DDL in-force rule, `restates`, `line-groups`, readings, method and run columns. Any M2 sentence that needs a target column is struck until the column exists. No new conceptual machinery until a replay report exists for the 254.
3. Split the product from the reconstruction. Cautious figure or publisher-stated figure as the only served total; inclusive matches and residuals in an annex; occurrence candidates specified with a blocking rule; M3b split so a citable line release is not hostage to accounts.
4. Put legal acts in milestone order. Private verbatim ledger, no third-party byte store, no hosted prompts, no public extract deposit, until the agreements and the per-table database-right assessment exist. Public-only registration accounts.
5. Re-price the actual reader-plus-arbiter protocol on ten hard documents; void a discovery campaign stopped by money; capture every admitted URL in a public archive at fetch time; scope F19 and C10 so Senegal’s late CRS years are not an implied failure of the record.

## Keep

Append-only snapshots cited by hash, not URL. Supersession instead of erasure, and correction as a new release that does not move the old DOI. World time kept apart from knowledge time, with a later discovery forbidden to rewrite K. Strict scope never filled from the extended scope; no cross-country sums; financial states not added; no silent FX; unknown not zero. Restatement is persistence, not corroboration. Unreachable, blocked, not published and loss of visibility kept distinct. Known-item list frozen, hidden, and not drawn from the trackers used to measure traceability. Parsers that refuse an unfamiliar layout and fail on printed totals. Locator checks that reject a quote the bytes do not contain. The legal note’s one-basis-per-act split and its open list for the DAJ and DPO, provided it is never cited as clearance. The refusal to adopt a graph store, OWL, or LinkML with no consumer.

## What most threatens the central claim

The central claim is that one researcher, with LLM assistance and no item-level human review, can release a frozen, neutral, citable record of what was promised, signed and paid, which journalists, researchers and negotiators can trust, and which still answers that question in 2030.

1. Correctness is unmeasured where it matters. Overlapping verbal probabilities, an unfillable calibration design, no release-blocking error rate, and no human read of principal documents or of the Vietnamese scan mean a cited total can be wrong while every specified test is green.
2. The money question the system is for is the question the fusion rules refuse to answer, and the storage layer cannot yet record the distinctions (restatement, occurrence, in-force chain) those rules need. Users will get either a blocked account or a number the spec does not actually control.
3. The record may be unlawful to distribute, or unverifiable once distributed, before the institutional conditions the legal note itself treats as preconditions are met; and the default horizon ends before the structured comparators can confirm the end of the partnership periods the dataset is supposed to judge.
